title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Competitive Methods - QBS
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Under the Brooks Act principles, Qualification-Based Selection (QBS) strictly mandates that which of the following cannot be used as an initial evaluation criterion?
questions.explain: The Brooks Act requires that Architecture and Engineering (A&E) firms be evaluated and ranked strictly on their technical qualifications before price is ever considered or negotiated.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: During a Qualification-Based Selection (QBS) process, the procurement officer successfully ranks the firms. The agency begins price negotiations with the highest-ranked firm, but they cannot agree on a fair and reasonable price. What is the buyer's required next step?
options: Cancel the solicitation and start over
Ask the top three firms to submit priced best and final offers (BAFOs)
Formally terminate negotiations with the top firm and open negotiations with the second-ranked firm
Accept the highest-ranked firm's price because qualifications matter more than budget
questions.explain: In QBS, if a fair and reasonable price cannot be negotiated with the highest-ranked firm, negotiations must be formally terminated with that firm, and the agency then proceeds to negotiate with the second-ranked firm.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which federal law originally mandated Qualification-Based Selection (QBS) for the procurement of architectural and engineering (A&E) services?
questions.explain: The Brooks Act of 1972 established the requirement that the U.S. Federal Government must select engineering and architecture firms based upon their competency, qualifications and experience rather than by price.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following professional services is nearly universally required by public procurement law to be procured via Qualification-Based Selection (QBS)?
questions.explain: Due to the Brooks Act and similar 'mini-Brooks Acts' at state/local levels, Architecture and Engineering (A&E) services must be procured using QBS.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Why is price excluded from the initial phase of Qualification-Based Selection (QBS)?
options: To ensure engineers are paid above market rate
To prevent agencies from knowing how much a project will cost
Because evaluating complex design competence and public safety should prioritize qualifications over finding the cheapest architect
Because price evaluation is illegal in all forms of public procurement
questions.explain: The Brooks Act asserts that in A&E work, public safety and design integrity are paramount. Prioritizing lowest cost could compromise safety and design quality, so competence must be established first.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: When performing Qualification-Based Selection (QBS) under the Brooks Act, if an agency reaches an impasse with the first-ranked firm over price, what must occur before negotiating with the second firm?
options: The second firm must lower their price below the first firm's offer
The agency must formally and in writing terminate negotiations with the first firm
The agency must combine the top two firms into a joint venture
questions.explain: An agency cannot bounce back and forth between vendors in QBS. They must formally end negotiations with the #1 firm before opening talks with #2. Once ended, they cannot go back to #1.
